Subject: Brightlane annual prepay cadence and automated drawdown tracker

Hi Oliver —

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Per our discussion I put together a lightweight proposal for how Redwood and Brightlane can operationalize the annual prepay / committed spend so your finance team has predictable invoice cadence and a minimal reconciliation surface. Key highlights in the attached workbook:

- Initial activation invoice: one-time invoice for the committed amount (or agreed upfront tranche).
- Ongoing drawdowns: automated monthly drawdown CSVs generated from usage with a single reconciliation invoice per month.
- VAT handling: separate evidence folder by entity and an EU VAT ID field on each invoice line for reverse-charge where applicable.
- PO and remit: we need your PO number and remit account/currency to populate the invoice footer and SEPA/SWIFT fields.

Action items for Brightlane: please confirm
1) PO number to reference on all invoices
2) VAT ID to appear on invoices (and whether reverse-charge applies)
3) preferred remit currency (EUR) and bank last 4 digits for routing confirmation

I attached: annual-prepay-invoice-schedule.xlsx (tabbed: cadence, drawdown-logic, VAT-asks) and a sample-invoice-brightlane.pdf. If that looks good we can:
- enable the automated drawdown sheet (shared Google sheet)
- create a DocuSign amendment to the existing SOW to capture PO + billing terms

Thanks — want to get this locked before month-end so accounting can plan the quarterly close.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Manager, Revenue Ops
Redwood Inference

Soojin / Jonas —

Couple operational notes after reviewing Oliver's replies and the workbook:

1) Invoice numbering: Redwood will issue an activation invoice numbered RI-2026-BL-001; subsequent monthly drawdown invoices will be RI-2026-BL-MMM (where MMM is month number). Put PO BL-PO-2026-0897 on all.
2) VAT flows: for EU clients that elect reverse-charge we should include a note on the invoice with the customer VAT and the following line: "Reverse charge – article 44 VAT Directive". Tag the invoice metadata so accounting can run the EU VAT report.
3) File formats: attach both PDF invoice and a machine-readable CSV for AP ingestion (columns: invoice_number, invoice_date, description, net_amount, vat_amount, gross_amount, customer_vat_id, po_number, bank_account_last4).

I've attached proposed-invoice-template.csv (CSV stub) and a short checklist for month-end reconciliation. Jonas: can you confirm the drawdown automation schedule (run on 1st of month UTC?) and retention policy for the CSVs?

Kimberly Park
Director, Billing Operations

Hi all —

Following the inputs from Brightlane and the ops team, this is the final cadence we will implement: 

- Activation: Invoice RI-2026-BL-001 issued on signature for the committed amount (applies if customer chooses full upfront).
- Monthly drawdown: automated CSV generated on the 1st UTC reflecting prior month usage; invoice issued on the 3rd UTC and emailed to ap@brightlane.co with PDF + CSV attachment.
- VAT: include customer VAT ID, reverse-charge note where Brightlane indicates EU reverse-charge. Redwood Accounting will tag these for quarterly VAT reporting.
- PO: BL-PO-2026-0897 on all documents.
- Remit verification: Brightlane to confirm bank last 4 digits (Oliver confirmed 3321) and currency EUR.
